exact_replacements.after: $G_e$ is the unit group of the full finite-dimensional associative centralizer algebra $C_e=\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C[e]}(V)=\{b:be=eb\}$. Its units are exactly $\{b\in C_e:\det b\ne0\}$: if $b$ commutes with $e$ and is invertible on $V$, its inverse also commutes with $e$. This is a nonempty open subset of the affine vector space $C_e$, containing the identity, so $G_e$ is smooth, irreducible and connected; no product-of-matrix-algebras identification is needed

exact_replacements.after: 2.1 Regularity of $F$ on $O$. The ranks of $X^0,X^1,\dots,X^{l-1}$ are constant on $O$. Cover $O$ by open charts where fixed minors used to select bases of the kernels and images, their quotient complements and Jordan top vectors are nonzero. Gaussian elimination on such a chart gives a Jordan basis for $X$ with entries regular in $X$. Let $g(X)$ carry a fixed Jordan basis for $e$ to this chosen Jordan basis for $X$, with the same ordered string lengths. Then $g(X)e g(X)^{-1}=X$. Restricting to the open chart where the Jordan-basis determinant is nonzero makes both $g(X)$ and $g(X)^{-1}$ regular, since their entries have only the fixed nonvanishing minors and determinant as denominators. Thus $X\mapsto(g(X)^{\otimes d})B(g(X)^{-1})^{\otimes d}$ is the map of step 1.2 and is regular on each chart. These charts cover $O$; on overlaps $g_2(X)^{-1}g_1(X)\in G_e$, so the expressions agree by $G_e$-invariance of $B$. Hence $F$ is regular on $O$. [F1, step 1.2, algebra, construct]
